questions.question: Your body can only get rid of alcohol through:
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: To get the most protection from a helmet, choose one that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. Helmets should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Only for use if the rear brake fails.

questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used correctly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides most of your stopping power.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so no need to worry.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be deadly.

questions.question: If you think your motorcycle will take longer to stop than usual, you should:

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase the distance between you and other vehicles on slippery surfaces. This gives you more room to stop safely.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it hard to control your motorcycle and should be avoided.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Wearing a helmet:

options.text: Increases the risk of neck injury.
Reduces the risk of neck injury.
Improves your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Improves your chances of surviving a crash.
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet reduces head and neck injuries and is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash. Any DOT-approved helmet lets you see clearly to the sides for safe riding.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle will work properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small mechanical problem can be more serious on a motorcycle than on a car. Always inspect your motorcycle before riding.

questions.question: The correct riding position is one where:

options.text: You sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
You sit as far back as possible and have to stretch to reach the grips.
You lean forward over the bike and use your arms to hold yourself up.
Your knees are kept far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward so your arms bend slightly when holding the grips. This lets you easily reach and operate the controls.

questions.question: Which fabric gives riders the best protection?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Before riding a motorcycle, you should check all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If a friend has had too much to drink and wants to ride a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have drunk too much. Stop them from riding by taking their keys if needed. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: When adjusting your rearview mirror, make sure you can see:

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirror to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. Your mirror may show a bit of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: Before each ride, make sure:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes cause friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever separately before every ride. Make sure each one feels firm and can hold the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: A good riding jacket should:

options.text: Not be worn in warm weather.

questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket made of leather when riding. Your clothing should be snug enough to not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it limits your movement. Wear protective clothing even in hot weather. Many riding jackets are designed to keep you cool.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are usually rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to leave the road faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, ease off the throttle and keep going straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: When choosing clothes for riding, which is NOT a good choice?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles.
A baseball cap to cover your hair.

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair.
questions.explanation: For safety, wear a DOT helmet, face or eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of strong material, sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: From ahead or behind, a motorcycle is _______ than a car.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's outline is much smaller than a car's. This makes it easy for other drivers to miss you on the road.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front.
Do not use your rearview mirrors to check traffic behind you.
Look for chances to ride through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front.
questions.explanation: Stay back from the vehicle ahead, even when stopped. This gives you room to move if the vehicle backs up or another vehicle comes at you quickly from behind.

questions.question: What material gives the best protection in riding gloves?
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another tough material to protect your hands.

questions.question: How often should you check your motorcycle before riding?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to avoid safety problems. Small issues on a motorcycle can be more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Use your headlight only when it is cloudy.
Use your headlight if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: Always ride with your headlight on, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after having one drink, can you ride safely?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and driving.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Alcohol effects may still be in your system.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be in your system.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system and affect your ability to ride safely.
